The decisive mistake was made by ProblemSolving_Expert at step 2. It rewrote the extracted fractions into simplified forms (2/4→1/2, 5/35→1/7, 30/5→6) and presented that as the final answer, even though the task asks for the fractions as they appear in the image, in order. That dropped the original fractions and produced a six-item list instead of the much longer correct answer. Verification_Expert then confirmed the wrong list at step 6 without checking it against the image. The OCR at step 1 also missed many fractions, but the failure that made the final answer wrong originated in step 2.
